s01.text: In a mixture of experts, a router decides which experts handle a token.

s02.text: It is a small network, trained to send tokens to the experts that handle them best.

s03.text: Which is the whole problem. If every token goes to the best-fitting expert, one expert wins.

s04.text: It gets all the training signal. The others get nothing, and they go stale.

s05.text: So the router is given a second objective: send a balanced share of tokens everywhere.

s06.text: That is the load-balancing loss, added to the training loss.

s07.text: It is a hack in the truest sense. The router is told to do something other than the thing it was built for.

s08.text: And the tension is real. Fit the tokens perfectly and the experts go stale. Balance them perfectly and the routing goes bad.

s09.text: So every router sits somewhere on that trade-off.

s10.text: Push too hard and the router starts sending tokens to worse experts, to satisfy the balance.

s11.text: Push too little and you are back to one popular expert doing all the work.

s12.text: The coefficient on that loss is the knob. One number trades quality against capacity.

s13.text: The router is trained to be good at routing, and punished for being good at it.
